analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Real Madrid (33 pts, five straight league wins) host Alaves (9th, 16 pts) on Saturday night, and the numbers make Madrid strong favourites with about 3.2 goals. Jose Mourinho's side came from behind to beat PSV 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday (Valverde, Bellingham, Mbappe twice, Vinicius), and with three away games next (Real Sociedad, Athletic, Arsenal) previews expect some rotation: Konate and Huijsen back in defence, Guler possibly in for Bernardo Silva. Rodrygo and Endrick are out and counted by the numbers; Mendy and Asencio are also out but have been for weeks, so Madrid's recent games already reflect it. Quique Sanchez's Alaves are without Facundo Garces and Mikel Rodriguez (season) and Hugo Novoa (counted), may rotate Rebbach (one booking from a ban), and one preview flags Angel Perez's availability as unclear. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.5 for Madrid, already raised for Madrid's 18 goals in their last six (+3.5%). The 5-1 against PSV shows the attack is in form, and even with rotation Mbappe, Vinicius, Bellingham and Guler give Madrid plenty; Rodrygo and Endrick are already counted. Alaves' attack depends partly on Angel Perez, whose availability one preview questions but nobody confirms, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already lowered because Alaves have won few corners lately and Madrid concede few (-6.0% on Alaves' side). Madrid's wide players (Vinicius, Diomande) keep their share steady whoever starts, so rotation changes little and I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, 2.8 for Alaves, already lowered for Madrid's quiet recent record (-3.7%). Alaves' Rebbach is one booking from a ban and may be rested, but that is minor, and no referee is named yet. Alaves are comfortable mid-table, with no sign of extra tension, so I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, already raised for Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+7.2%). Mourinho may rotate after PSV and before three away games, but Madrid's depth keeps their output high and the extra rest of a home game helps, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, already lifted for Madrid's sharp recent finishing (47 on target in six, +5.6%). Alaves keep their usual goalkeeper and back line apart from long-term absentee Garces, and possible changes (Valentini for Jonny) are like-for-like. Nothing new, so I stay at about 10.2.
